title: The 4 Best Panini Presses and Sandwich Makers Under $60
h1: The 4 Best Panini Presses and Sandwich Makers Under $60
metaDescription: Our 4 picks for panini presses and sandwich makers under $60, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at panini presses and sandwich makers under $60 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Panini Press 25460A
products.blurb: Key specs: Floating hinge opens 180 degrees, 8-inch by 10-inch nonstick grids, Locking latch for storage.
strengths: Floating hinge is the key upgrade at this price, adjusts to thick and unevenly loaded sandwiches
8x10 grid fits larger sandwiches and tortillas than budget clamshell units
180-degree opening doubles as a flat grill for burgers, bacon, or vegetables
limitations: No temperature dial, still runs at one fixed heat
Grids aren't removable for deep cleaning

products.name: Proctor Silex Deluxe Hot Sandwich Maker
products.blurb: Key specs: Fits 2 sandwiches at once, Ceramic nonstick plates, 700W element.
strengths: Ceramic nonstick plates perform well for basic sandwiches and quesadillas
Smaller footprint than the Hamilton Beach if storage space is tight
limitations: Fixed clamshell gap, no floating hinge
Smaller plates than the Hamilton Beach

products.name: Cuisinart GR-4N 5-in-1 Griddler
limitations: Drip tray small for fatty foods

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
